rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expresses the hope that the people might warm themselves by the fire; ṣilāʾ means a great fire.
rows.anchor: رجاء أن تستدفئوا بها والصلاء النار العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the call carries the force of speech, أن بورك can be rendered simply بورك; alternatively أن is a verbal noun particle or a light form of أنّ.
rows.anchor: فإن النداء فيه معنى القول، أو ب { أن بورك } على أنها مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a light أنّ normally requires a compensatory لا، قد، سـ، or سوف, this is a supplication and differs from ordinary cases.
rows.anchor: والتخفيف وإن اقتضى التعويض بلا أو قد أو السين أو سوف لكنه دعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent is everyone in that land, the valley, and its surroundings in Syria, blessed as the abode and burial place of prophets, especially the place where God spoke to Moses.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه عام في كل من تلك الأرض، وفي ذلك الواد وحواليها من أرض الشام الموسومة بالبركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies those in and around the fire as Moses and the angels who were present.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد موسى والملائكة الحاضرون، وتصدير الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening address gives glad tidings that a momentous affair has been decreed whose blessing will spread through Syria.
rows.anchor: بشارة بأنه قد قضى له أمر عظيم تنتشر بركته في أقطار الشأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glorification is part of the call, guarding listeners from imagining that hearing God's speech implies likeness between God and creation, and expressing wonder at the affair's greatness.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم من سماع كلامه تشبيها وللتعجيب من عظمة ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses himself exclaimed in wonder at the greatness of what had happened.
rows.anchor: أو تعجب من موسى لما دهاه من عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the address to Moses, the هاء may be the pronoun of the matter followed by an explanatory sentence; alternatively it refers to the speaker, with أنا as predicate and الله as its explication.
rows.anchor: الهاء للشأن و { أنا الله } جملة مفسرة له، أو للمتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العزيز الحكيم prepares for the sign to come: God is powerful enough to do what seems impossible, such as turning a staff into a serpent, and acts with wisdom and order.
rows.anchor: صفتان لله ممهدتان لما أراد أن يظهره، يريد أنا القوي القادر على ما يبعد من الأوهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to cast down the staff is coordinated with the earlier blessing announcement; the repeated أن after the address to Moses supports this parsing.
rows.anchor: أي نودي أن بورك من في النار وأن ألق عصاك، ويدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jān is a light, swiftly moving serpent.
rows.anchor: حية خفيفة سريعة، وقرىء «جأن» على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading جأن follows the language of someone who intensifies avoidance of two adjacent sukūns while fleeing.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «جأن» على لغة من جد في الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned and did not come back; عَقَّب is used of a fighter who turns back after fleeing.
rows.anchor: ولم يرجع من عقب المقاتل إذا كر بعد الفرار، وإنما رعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was terrified because he thought the strange event was directed against him, as the reassurance not to fear indicates.
rows.anchor: وإنما رعب لظنه أن ذلك الأمر أريد به ويدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reassurance may mean do not fear anyone besides Me, trusting in Me, or may be unrestricted.
rows.anchor: أي من غيري ثقة بي أو مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers do not fear while receiving revelation because of their absorption in it, although they are the people most fearful of God.
rows.anchor: أي حين يوحى إليهم من فرط الاستغراق فإنهم أخوف الناس أي من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, messengers have no fear of ending badly in God's presence.
rows.anchor: أو لا يكون لهم عندي سوء عاقبة فيخافون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen explains her proposed reconciliation: she will send envoys bearing a gift to deflect Solomon from taking her kingdom.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إني مرسلة رسلا بهدية أدفعه بها عن ملكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She will assess Solomon's disposition from the envoys' return and then decide what to do.
rows.anchor: من حاله حتى أعمل بحسب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says she sent Minḏir b. ʿAmr with disguised boys and girls, a pearl and crooked bead as tests; informed by Gabriel, Solomon used worms and water to solve them, then returned the gift.
rows.anchor: روي أنها بعثت منذر بن عمرو في وفد وأرسلت معهم غلمانا على زي الجواري وجواري على زي الغلمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What came to Solomon may be the messenger or the gift itself.
rows.anchor: أي الرسول أو ما أهدت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the plural جاؤوا.
rows.anchor: أو ما أهدت إليه وقرىء «فلما جاؤوا»

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Hamza and Yaʿqūb read the nūns with assimilation.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings have one nūn, two nūns, or deletion of the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بنون واحدة وبنونين وحذف الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke addresses the messenger and his companions, or the messenger and the queen, with the addressed envoy standing for the sender.
rows.anchor: خطاب للرسول ومن معه، أو للرسول والمرسل على تغليب المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God gave Solomon is prophethood and a kingdom beyond comparison, so he has no need of their gift and it has no value to him.
rows.anchor: من النبوة والملك الذي لا مزيد عليه

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read the yāʾ in آتاني with fatḥ; others give it sukūn, and al-Kisāʾī alone uses imāla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص بفتح الياء والباقون بإسكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They delight in gifts because they know only outward worldly life and love increasing their wealth.
rows.anchor: لأنكم لا تعلمون إلا ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا فتفرحون بما يهدى إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they rejoice in what they give because they take pride before their peers.
rows.anchor: أو بما تهدونه افتخارا على أمثالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turn shifts from rejecting and belittling the payment to explaining why they offered it: they assume Solomon shares their limited worldly ambition.
rows.anchor: والإضراب عن إنكار الإمداد بالمال عليه وتقليله إلى بيان السبب الذي حملهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends to favor the oppressed by rescuing them from Pharaoh's oppression.
rows.anchor: أن نتفضل عليهم بإنقاذهم من بأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ونريد recounts a past state, coordinated with Pharaoh's rise as part of explaining the report, or it is circumstantial from يستضعف; the intended favor need not coincide with the oppression.
rows.anchor: حكاية حال ماضية معطوفة على { إن فرعون علا فى الأرض } من حيث إنهما واقعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parsing makes ونريد circumstantial from يستضعف; God's will can concern a future result even while the oppression is occurring.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم من مقارنة الإرادة للاستضعاف مقارنة المراد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressed are to become leaders in religious affairs and inherit what Pharaoh and his people possessed.
rows.anchor: أئمة } مقدمين في أمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land means Egypt and Syria; تمكين originally means giving something a place where it can settle, then by metaphor giving it dominion.
rows.anchor: أرض مصر والشام، وأصل التمكين أن تجعل للشيء مكانا يتمكن فيه ثم استعير للتسليط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will show Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies through the Israelites what they feared: loss of rule and destruction at the hands of a child born among them.
rows.anchor: من ذهاب ملكهم وهلاكهم على يد مولود منهم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read يري with yāʾ and put Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { ويري } بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation to Moses' mother came either by inspiration or in a dream.
rows.anchor: بإلهام أو رؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She should nurse him while concealment is possible, place him in the Nile if she fears discovery, and neither fear his loss nor grieve: God will soon return him safely and make him a messenger.
rows.anchor: ما أمكنك إخفاؤه. { فإذا خفت عليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a midwife at Moses' birth saw light between his eyes, was moved to love him and did not inform; his mother nursed him three months, then hid him in a chest and cast it into the Nile as Pharaoh intensified the search.
rows.anchor: فلما وقع موسى على الأرض هالها نور بين عينيه وارتعشت مفاصلها ودخل حبه في قلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about his becoming their enemy and grief explains the outcome of their taking him, presented as though it were their motive.
rows.anchor: تعليل لالتقاطهم إياه بما هو عاقبته ومؤداه تشبيها له بالغرض الحامل عليه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read حزنًا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { وحزنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were wrong in everything: after killing thousands to find Moses, they raised him to maturity so he could do what they feared; the sentence emphasizes their error or explains their affliction.
rows.anchor: في كل شيء فليس ببدع منهم أن قتلوا ألوفا لأجله ثم أخذوه يربونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were sinners, and God punished them by having them raise their enemy themselves.
rows.anchor: أو مذنبين فعاقبهم الله تعالى بأن ربى عدوهم على أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading خاطين lightens خطئين; another has خاطين, those who make error in place of correctness.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «خاطين» تخفيف { خطئين } أو «خاطين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enemy of both Moses and the Israelite was not of their religion, and the Egyptians were enemies of the Israelites.
rows.anchor: لموسى والإسرائيلي لأنه لم يكن على دينهما ولأن القبط كانوا أعداء لبني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الإسرائيلي
rows.claim: One view says the Israelite spoke, having assumed Moses would strike him after Moses called him misguided.
rows.anchor: قاله الإسرائيلي لأنه لما سماه غويا ظن أنه يبطش عليه

rows.speaker: القبطي
rows.claim: Another view says the Egyptian spoke, supposing Moses had killed an Egyptian the previous day on this Israelite's behalf.
rows.anchor: أو القبطي وكأنه توهم من قوله أنه الذي قتل القبطي بالأمس لهذا الإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن تريد here means ما تريد.
rows.anchor: ما تريد. { إلا أن تكون جبارا فى الأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A جبّار is one who dominates people and ignores the consequences.
rows.anchor: تطاول على الناس ولا تنظر في العواقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is accused of not being among those who reconcile people and settle disputes by the better course.
rows.anchor: فتدفع التخاصم بالتي هي أحسن، ولما قال هذا انتشر الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the accusation spread to Pharaoh and his council, who planned to kill Moses, a believer from Pharaoh's family, his cousin, came to warn him.
rows.anchor: وهموا بقتله فخرج مؤمن آل فرعون وهو ابن عمه ليخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يسعى means hastening; it is an adjective of رجل, or a circumstantial phrase if من أقصى المدينة is its adjective, not a complement of جاء because that qualification makes the noun definite-like.
rows.anchor: يسرع صفة رجل، أو حال منه إذا جعل من أقصى المدينة صفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are consulting about Moses; consultation is called يأتمر because each participant commands the others and follows their command.
rows.anchor: يتشاورون بسببك، وإنما سمي التشاور ائتمارا لأن كلا من المتشاورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لك clarifies the addressee; it is not governed by الناصحين, since a relative-clause complement cannot precede its relative.
rows.anchor: ل { النصحين } لأن معمول الصلة لا يتقدم الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses left the city afraid and watching for someone pursuing him; he prayed to be rescued and protected from the wrongdoers catching up.
rows.anchor: لحوق طالب. { قال رب نجني من القوم الظلمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian is opposite him, a village named for Midian son of Abraham and associated with Shuʿayb; it was outside Pharaoh's realm, eight days from Egypt.
rows.anchor: قبالة مدين قرية شعيب، سميت باسم مدين بن إبراهيم عليهم الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusting God and expecting good, Moses chose the middle of three routes without knowing the way; pursuers came after him and took the other two.
rows.anchor: وكان لا يعرف الطريق فعن له ثلاث طرق فأخذ في أوسطها وجاء الطلاب عقيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reached a well where a large group watered their livestock; the two women stood below them and kept their sheep away to avoid mixing with the flock.
rows.anchor: وصل إليه وهو بئر كانوا يسقون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women held their sheep back from the water; they waited until the shepherds moved their animals away to avoid crowding with men.
rows.anchor: تمنعان أغنامهما عن الماء لئلا تختلط بأغنامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of the women’s watering is omitted because the point is their modesty and the reason Moses would be prompted to water for them.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول لأن الغرض هو بيان ما يدل على عفتهما ويدعوه إلى السقي لهما

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read يصدر, meaning that the shepherds depart.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر »يصدر« أي ينصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has الرعاء with ḍamma; it is a collective noun like الرخال.
rows.anchor: وقرىء » الرعاء« بالضم وهو اسم جمع كالرخال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father was elderly and unable to go out to water the flock, so the women had to do it.
rows.anchor: كبير السن لا يستطيع أن يخرج للسقي فيرسلنا اضطرارا

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denies knowing another god, not that one exists: he had no basis for certainty about its nonexistence, so he orders the tower to investigate.
rows.anchor: نفى علمه بإله غيره دون وجوده إذ لم يكن عنده ما يقتضي الجزم بعدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He imagines that any god would be a body in the sky that could be reached by climbing.
rows.anchor: كأنه توهم أنه لو كان لكان جسما في السماء يمكن الترقي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he wanted an observatory to track celestial positions and learn whether they signaled a messenger's mission or a change of rule.
rows.anchor: أو أراد أن يبني له رصدا يترصد منه أوضاع الكواكب فيرى هل فيها ما يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says that he thinks Moses is lying.
rows.anchor: وإني لأظنه من الكذبين

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes denial of knowledge as denial of the known, as in the verse meaning that there are no gods in the heavens or earth; this inference applies to active knowledge, whose objects depend on it, unlike passive knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بنفي العلم نفي المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report calls Pharaoh the first to make fired brick; the order both teaches the craft and expresses grandeur, while the vocative يا Haman interrupts the sentence.
rows.anchor: قيل أول من اتخذ الآجر فرعون ولذلك أمر باتخاذه على وجه يتضمن تعليم الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance in the land was without right, meaning without deserving it.
rows.anchor: هو وجنوده فى الأرض بغير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought they would not return to God through resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read يرجعون with fatḥ on yāʾ and kasr on jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي بفتح الياء وكسر الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويوم يناديهم is coordinated with the Day of Resurrection, or it is governed by an implied اذكر.
rows.anchor: عطف على يوم القيامة أو منصوب باذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أين شركائي, the two objects of تزعمون are omitted: those you claimed to be My partners.
rows.anchor: أي الذين كنتم تزعمونهم شركائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those against whom the threat has taken effect face the fulfillment of God's threat to fill Hell with jinn and people, and other warning verses.
rows.anchor: لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In هؤلاء الذين أغوينا, a pronoun referring back to الذين is omitted.
rows.anchor: أغويناهم فحذف الراجع إلى الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went astray just as their leaders did, showing they chose freely; the leaders only whispered and enticed them.
rows.anchor: وهو استئناف للدلالة على أنهم غووا باختيارهم وأنهم لم يفعلوا بهم إلا وسوسة وتسويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes الذين an adjective and أغويناهم the predicate, adding information that becomes essential despite being formally supplementary.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { الذين } صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders disavow the followers and the disbelief they chose out of desire; this confirms the preceding statement.
rows.anchor: وهو تقرير للجملة المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confirmation is left uncoordinated with a conjunction.
rows.anchor: ولذلك خلت عن العاطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers did not worship the leaders; they worshipped their own desires.
rows.anchor: أي ما كانوا يعبدوننا، وإنما كانوا يعبدون أهواءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما is a verbal noun connected to تبرأنا: the leaders disavow the followers' worship of them.
rows.anchor: مصدرية متصلة ب { تبرأنا } أي تبرأنا من عبادتهم إيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call on their partners out of extreme bewilderment, but the partners cannot answer or help; the punishment is clinging to them.
rows.anchor: ورأوا العذاب } لازما بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They might wish they had found some stratagem to repel the punishment or had been guided to truth when they saw it.
rows.anchor: لوجه من الحيل يدفعون به العذاب، أو إلى الحق لما رأوا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لو expresses a wish here: they wished they had been guided.
rows.anchor: أي تمنوا أنهم كانوا مهتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about their answer to the messengers follows the question about associating partners: God first asks about shirk, then about denying the prophets.
rows.anchor: عطف على الأول فإنه تعالى يسأل أولا عن إشراكهم به ثم عن تكذيبهم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day their answers become inaccessible to them; they cannot find a response.
rows.anchor: فصارت الأنباء كالعمي عليهم لا تهتدي إليهم، وأصله فعموا عن الأنباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording reverses the expected relation for emphasis: what comes to mind is received from outside, and if it misses them they cannot summon it.
rows.anchor: لكنه عكس مبالغة ودلالة على أن ما يحضر الذهن إنما يقبض ويرد عليه من خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأنباء may mean their answers to the messengers or all reports generally; even messengers stammer under the terror and defer to God's knowledge, so the misguided are worse off.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأنباء ما أجابوا به الرسل أو ما يعمها وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is construed with على because it carries the sense of concealment.
rows.anchor: وتعدية الفعل بعلى لتضمنه معنى الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A witness from each community is its prophet, who testifies to what the people did.
rows.anchor: وهو نبيهم يشهد عليهم بما كانوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The communities are challenged to produce proof for their religion; they then realize that divinity belongs exclusively to God, and their fabrications disappear.
rows.anchor: على صحة ما كنتم تدينون به

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was Moses' cousin, son of Yaṣhar b. Qāhith b. Levi, and was among those who believed in Moses.
rows.anchor: كان ابن عمه يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوي وكان ممن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His transgression meant seeking superiority over his people and wanting them under his command, behaving arrogantly, or oppressing them.
rows.anchor: فطلب الفضل عليهم وأن يكونوا تحت أمره، أو تكبر عليهم أو ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says this occurred when Pharaoh put Qarun in charge of the Israelites.
rows.anchor: قيل وذلك حين ملكه فرعون على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Qarun envied Moses and Aaron, complaining that Moses had prophecy and Aaron priesthood while he had nothing; Moses replied that this was God's arrangement.
rows.anchor: لما روي أنه قال لموسى عليه السلام: لك الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasures were stored wealth.
rows.anchor: من الأموال المدخرة. { ما إن مفاتحه } مفاتيح صناديقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مفاتحه means the keys to his chests, from the singular مفتح with kasra, the tool used to open; alternatively it means his treasuries, from مفتح.
rows.anchor: مفاتيح صناديقه جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به، وقيل خزائنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys weigh heavily on a strong band of people; تنوء means to bear a load that bends or inclines someone.
rows.anchor: والجملة صلة وهو ثاني مفعولي آتى، ونائبه الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has لينوء with yāʾ, giving the genitive complement the syntactic status of its governing noun.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «لينوء» بالياء على إعطاء المضاف حكم المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause إذ قال له قومه is governed by تنوء.
rows.anchor: { إذ قال له قومه } منصوب ب «تنوء»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا تفرح means do not become arrogant in worldly joy; it is blameworthy because worldly pleasure departs, and knowing it must end brings grief. The verse links this to 57:23.
rows.anchor: لا تبطر والفرح بالدنيا مذموم مطلقا لأنه نتيجة حبها والرضا بها والذهول عن ذهابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love those exulting in worldly ornament; such joy blocks love of God.
rows.anchor: وعلل النهي ها هنا بكونه مانعا من محبة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the wealth God gave you to seek the afterlife, spending it on what secures it; wealth is meant as a means to the next life.
rows.anchor: بصرفه فيما يوجبها لك فإن المقصود منه أن يكون وصلة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not neglect your share of this world: use it to attain the afterlife and take what suffices for you.
rows.anchor: ولا تترك ترك المنسي. { نصيبك من الدنيا } وهو أن تحصل بها آخرتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do good to God's servants as God has shown goodness to you.
rows.anchor: إلى عباد الله. { كما أحسن الله إليك } فيما أنعم الله عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to do good through gratitude and obedience, as God did good through His gifts.
rows.anchor: وقيل { أحسن } بالشكر والطاعة { كما أحسن } إليك بالإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not cause corruption by any act that leads to injustice or transgression; the command rebukes Qarun's prior wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: بأمر يكون علة للظلم والبغي، نهي له عما كان عليه من الظلم والبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love corrupters because of their evil actions.
rows.anchor: لسوء أفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun claims his knowledge made him superior to others and entitled him to status and wealth; علم is circumstantial and may mean Torah knowledge, in which he excelled.
rows.anchor: فضلت به على الناس واستوجبت به التفوق عليهم بالجاه والمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed meanings of his claimed knowledge are alchemy, trade and estate management, or knowledge of Joseph's treasures.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الكيمياء وقيل علم التجارة والدهقنة وسائر المكاسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عندي may describe the knowledge or attach to أوتيته, meaning according to my belief or opinion.
rows.anchor: صفة له أو متعلق ب { أوتيته } كقولك: جاز هذا عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes Qarun for boasting in strength and wealth despite knowing that stronger and richer past nations were destroyed; he had read or heard their histories.
rows.anchor: تعجب وتوبيخ على اغتراره بقوته وكثرة ماله مع علمه بذلك لأنه قرأه في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question rebuts his claim to knowledge: did he lack the knowledge of history that could have protected him from their fate?
rows.anchor: أو رد لادعائه للعلم وتعظمه به بنفي هذا العلم عنه أي أعنده مثل ذلك العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are not asked to supply information because God knows their sins, or to be rebuked because punishment comes suddenly; God knows and will punish all sinners.
rows.anchor: سؤال استعلام فإنه تعالى مطلع عليها أو معاتبة فإنهم يعذبون بها بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Qarun harassed Moses, agreed to pay one in a thousand after the zakat command, then plotted to discredit him by bribing a woman to accuse him falsely; Moses summoned her and she exposed Qarun's bribe.
rows.anchor: روي أنه كان يؤذي موسى عليه السلام كل وقت وهو يداريه لقرابته حتى نزلت الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the report, Moses prayed after the false accusation was exposed; God commanded the earth to take Qarun, who sank in stages while pleading, and God rebuked Moses for not showing mercy.
rows.anchor: فأوحى إليه أن مر الأرض بما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Israelites said Moses had done this to inherit Qarun's wealth, Moses prayed to God, who caused Qarun's house and possessions to sink as well.
rows.anchor: ثم قال بنو إسرائيل: إنما فعله ليرثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A فئة is a group of helpers, from a verb meaning to incline or bend something.
rows.anchor: أعوان مشتقة من فأوت رأسه إذا ميلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No group could rescue Qarun by warding off God's punishment.
rows.anchor: { ينصرونه من دون الله } فيدفعون عنه عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He could not defend himself: one who defeats an enemy is said to help and then prevail against him.
rows.anchor: الممتنعين منه من قولهم نصره من عدوه فانتصر إذا منعه منه فامتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إبراهيم may be coordinated with Noah, be an object of an implied اذكر, or be nominative with an implied ومن المرسلين إبراهيم.
rows.anchor: عطف على { نوحا } أو نصب بإضمار اذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is attached to أرسلنا: Abraham was sent when his judgment matured and he recognized the truth; alternatively it is an appositional substitute if اذكر is understood.
rows.anchor: ظرف لأرسلنا أي أرسلناه حين كمل عقله وتم نظره بحيث عرف الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham told his people to worship God and fear Him because that is better than their current practice, if they can distinguish good from evil or reason with knowledge rather than ignorance.
rows.anchor: الخير والشر وتميزون ما هو خير مما هو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They worship idols and fabricate claims by calling them gods and alleging that they intercede with God.
rows.anchor: وتكذبون كذبا في تسميتها آلهة وادعاء شفاعتها عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they make and carve the idols for the sake of falsehood; the phrase shows their practice is vile because it is fraud and untruth.
rows.anchor: أو تعملونها وتنحتونها للإفك وهو استدلال على شرارة ما هم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include form II, suggesting repeated making, and form V, suggesting affected or pretended making.
rows.anchor: وقرىء »تخلقون« من خلق للتكثير »وتخلقون« من تخلق للتكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إفكًا may be a verbal noun like الكذب or an adjective meaning a creation laden with falsehood.
rows.anchor: و { إفكا } على أنه مصدر كالكذب أو نعت بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second argument against the idols: they cannot bring any benefit by providing sustenance.
rows.anchor: دليل ثان على شرارة ذلك من حيث إنه لا يجدي بطائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رزقًا may be an infinitive, meaning they cannot provide, or the thing provided; its indefinite form is general.
rows.anchor: يحتمل المصدر بمعنى لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek all sustenance from God, since He owns it.
rows.anchor: كله فإنه المالك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and gratitude are means to obtain what you need and a way to acknowledge the blessings you have received.
rows.anchor: متوسلين إلى مطالبكم بعبادته مقيدين لما حفكم من النعم بشكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, worship and gratitude prepare people to meet God.
rows.anchor: أو مستعدين للقائه بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has fatḥ on the tāʾ in ترجعون.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they reject Muhammad, earlier peoples also rejected their messengers; their denial harmed themselves by bringing punishment, and this people's denial will do the same.
rows.anchor: من قبلي من الرسل فلم يضرهم تكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's duty is only to convey clearly enough to remove doubt, not to ensure that people believe.
rows.anchor: الذي يزال معه الشك وما عليه أن يصدق ولا يكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage may continue Abraham's story through his people's answer, or be a digression about Muhammad and Quraysh that refutes their doctrine and consoles him through the parallel with Abraham.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون اعتراضا بذكر شأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقريش وهدم مذهبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot is coordinated with Abraham or with the phrase to which Abraham is coordinated.
rows.anchor: عطف على إبراهيم أو على ما عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indecent act is an action at the extreme of ugliness.
rows.anchor: لتأتون الفحشة } الفعلة البالغة في القبح

rows.speaker: الحرميان وابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: Al-Ḥaramiyyān, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ read the first question with a kasra hamza as a statement; the others read it as a question, and all agree the second is interrogative.
rows.anchor: وقرأالحرميان وابن عامر وحفص بهمزة مكسورة على الخبر والباقون على الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one had committed this before them; the fact that natural instincts recoil from it confirms its abomination and points to their corrupt disposition.
rows.anchor: استئناف مقرر لفاحشتها من حيث إنها مما اشمأزت منه الطباع وتحاشت عنه النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have sex with men and cut off the road by attacking travelers, killing and robbing them, or raping them until routes are blocked.
rows.anchor: وتتعرضون للسابلة بالقتل وأخذ المال أو بالفاحشة حتى انقطعت الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they cut off procreation by turning away from women and having sex that cannot produce offspring.
rows.anchor: أو تقطعون سبيل النسل بالإعراض عن الحرث وإتيان ما ليس بحرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nādī is an assembly while its people are gathered in it.
rows.anchor: في مجالسكم الغاصة بأهلها ولا يقال للنادي إلا لما فيه أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reprehensible acts include sex, farting, exposing clothing, and other shameless behaviors.
rows.anchor: كالجماع والضراط وحل الإزار وغيرها من القبائح عدم مبالاة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the public misconduct as hذف, throwing small stones or pellets.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحذف ورمي البنادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for divine punishment challenges either Lot's judgment that their conduct is vile or the prophethood implied by his rebuke.
rows.anchor: في استقباح ذلك أو في دعوى النبوة المفهومة من التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These parables and similar examples bring difficult ideas within people's understanding; only people who think carefully grasp their benefit.
rows.anchor: ولا يعقل حسنها وفائدتها. { إلا العلمون } الذين يتدبرون الأشياء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet defined a learned person as one who understands what God wants, obeys Him, and avoids what incurs His displeasure.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تلا هذه الآية فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the heavens and earth purposefully, not in vain; their intended benefit is to point to His essence and attributes, a sign for believers who benefit from it.
rows.anchor: محقا غير قاصد به باطلا، فإن المقصود بالذات من خلقها إفادة الخير والدلالة على ذاته وصفاته

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite revelation to draw near to God, preserve its wording, and uncover its meanings; repeated attentive reading may reveal what was not clear at first hearing.
rows.anchor: تقربا إلى الله تعالى بقراءته وتحفظا لألفاظه واستكشافا لمعانيه، فإن القارىء المتأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing by prompting avoidance during prayer and at other times, since it recalls God and instills fear of Him.
rows.anchor: بأن تكون سببا للانتهاء عن المعاصي حال الاشتغال بها وغيرها من حيث إنها تذكر الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report tells of an Anṣārī youth who prayed with the Prophet yet committed grave sins; the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him, and he soon repented.
rows.anchor: مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلوات ولا يدع شيئا من الفواحش إلا ارتكبه، فوصف له عليه السلام فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is greater than other acts of worship; it is called remembrance because remembrance is the main reason for its virtue and its restraint of sin.
rows.anchor: وللصلاة أكبر من سائر الطاعات، وإنما عبر عنها به للتعليل بأن اشتمالها على ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God's merciful remembrance of people is greater than their remembrance of Him through obedience.
rows.anchor: أو لذكر الله إياكم برحمته أكبر من ذكركم إياه بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows prayer and all other acts of worship and rewards them with the best recompense.
rows.anchor: منه ومن سائر الطاعات فيجازيكم به أحسن المجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originates creation and then restores it through resurrection; people return to Him for judgment.
rows.anchor: ينشئهم. { ثم يعيده } يبعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to direct address emphasizes the intended point.
rows.anchor: والعدول إلى الخطاب للمبالغة في المقصود

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وأبو عمرو وروح
rows.claim: Abū Bakr, Abū ʿAmr, and Rawḥ read يرجعون in the third person, following the preceding wording.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر وأبو عمرو وروح بالياء على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals fall silent in perplexity and despair, as in the expression أبلس when someone becomes silent and loses hope of making an argument; a she-camel that does not bellow is also called مبلاس.
rows.anchor: ومنه الناقة المبلاس التي لا ترغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading opens the lām, from أبلسه, meaning he silenced him.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح اللام من أبلسه إذا أسكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners have no power to intercede and protect the idolaters from God's punishment; the past tense marks this as certain.
rows.anchor: يجيرونهم من عذاب الله، ومجيئه بلفظ الماضي لتحققه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they despair of their gods they disbelieve in them; alternatively, they were already unbelievers in worldly life because of them.
rows.anchor: يكفرون بآلهتهم حين يئسوا منهم، وقيل كانوا في الدنيا كافرين بسببهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf writes شفعاء with an added wāw, as it does علموا بني إسرائيل in 26:197 and السوأى with alif, reflecting the hamza's written form.
rows.anchor: بالواو وكذا { السوأى } بالألف إثباتا للهمزة على صورة الحرف
